scope.title: A closer look at storefront source
scope.description: Follow the declarations, inspect their metadata, then review what the browser still needs to verify.
scope.scripts: External scripts or modules, at most
scope.runtime: Browser registration and execution remain unverified.

checks.title: Know what each check tells you.
checks.description: Seven checks separate source findings, improvement opportunities, and the evidence that still needs a browser.
checks.workflowsNote: These eight workflows are useful review areas. A store does not need to expose every one through WebMCP.

items.discovery: Named declarations are recovered from HTML forms or registration code. An API reference alone leaves the available tool inventory unresolved.
items.metadata: Review tool names, descriptions, and possible duplicate names on the same page. Short descriptions are a quality suggestion, not a protocol failure.
items.parameters: Inspect recoverable input names, types, descriptions, and required state. A parameterless tool may omit its input schema; dynamic schemas can remain unresolved.
items.implementation: The source can show a declared handler or form operation. The scanner does not run the handler, submit the form, or confirm its behavior.
items.forms: Public forms can reveal adoption opportunities. Check existing tools first and preserve the form’s validation and consent; sensitive flows need manual review.
items.coverage: The report keeps blocked resources, failures, and scan limits visible. Unvisited pages, authenticated flows, and runtime-generated code can fall outside the inspected source.
items.runtime: This check remains unknown. Confirm native registration and behavior separately in a browser with WebMCP support; source findings cannot certify agent usage.
